index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a schematic overview of a channelwise autoencoder architecture designed for processing EEG data. The global layout is vertically structured, depicting a sequential flow from top to bottom: an input feature map F from the k−1th layer, a central processing block, and an output feature map G from the k−th layer. The entire diagram is enclosed within a clean, rectangular boundary with rounded corners, emphasizing a modular and hierarchical design.

At the top, the input feature map F is represented as a large rounded rectangle containing a list of channels labeled Channel 1 through Channel C, with ellipsis indicating intermediate channels. Each channel is visually depicted as a distinct, colored, wavy rectangular block—Channel 1 in purple, Channel 2 in yellow, Channel 3 in green, and Channel C in pink—symbolizing individual EEG channel data. These blocks are arranged horizontally, slightly overlapping, to suggest parallel processing while maintaining visual separation.

The central processing block is a larger rounded rectangle encompassing two main components: a 1D convolutional layer and an Add&LayerNorm module. The 1D convolutional layer is specified with 'groups=C', indicating grouped convolutions where each group corresponds to one channel, ensuring channel-wise independent processing. This component is shown as a rounded rectangle with bold black text. Below it, the Add&LayerNorm module is similarly styled, representing the residual connection and normalization step. A bidirectional arrow connects these two modules, signifying a feedback or residual loop between them, which is typical in transformer-like or residual network architectures.

A vertical arrow descends from the input feature map to the 1D convolutional layer, indicating the forward pass. From the Add&LayerNorm module, another arrow points downward to the output feature map G, which mirrors the input structure: a rounded rectangle listing Channel 1 to Channel C with corresponding colored wavy blocks, identical in style to the input but possibly reduced in size to reflect downsampling.

On the right side of the diagram, a horizontal line extends from the input feature map, labeled 'Downsample' along its length, and connects to the Add&LayerNorm module. This represents a skip connection or shortcut that performs spatial downsampling on the input before adding it to the processed output, preserving spatial information while reducing dimensionality.

The bottom of the diagram includes a caption stating 'Output feature map G from k − th layer', mirroring the top caption 'Input feature map F from k − 1th layer'. The overall color scheme is minimalistic, using black outlines and text with pastel-colored blocks for channels, enhancing clarity and focus on the architectural flow. The design emphasizes channel-wise independence, computational efficiency, and alignment with EEG data structure, as described in the figure caption.
